title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of §42 (manuscript p. 331), a 'récapitulation' or reference sheet. It fixes conventions for the rest of Grothendieck's work on the 'équation des lacets'. On the previous page that equation appears as ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 together with σ∞(φ(ξ))^{-1}φ(ξ)=ε1^r ξ^{-1} ε0^s. These are essentially the hexagon (order-3) and involution (order-2) relations of what is now called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

Title chain. The group 𝔊_{0,3} is identified successively with:
(i) the fundamental group of U_{0,3}^an = P^1(C) minus {0,1,∞}, made equivariant for the finite symmetry group, i.e. the orbifold/stack fundamental group of the quotient, based at the point -j̄ = e^{iπ/3} fixed by ρ;
(ii) the fundamental group of the orbifold P^1 with weights 0{0}+2{1}+3{∞}, i.e. a cusp and cone points of orders 2 and 3, the (2,3,∞) modular orbifold, extended by the real structure;
(iii) GL(2,Z)/{±1} = PGL(2,Z), written GP(1,Z);
(iv) T'_{1,1} = T_{1,1}/{±1}, where T_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z) is the extended mapping-class ('Teichmüller modular') group of the once-punctured torus, orientation-reversing classes included.
The section also announces a 'formulaire fondamental' for the 'loop automorphisms' of the profinite completions of 𝔊^+_{0,3} and π_{0,3}.

Part I. 𝔊_{0,3} is presented as an extension 1 → π_{0,3} → 𝔊_{0,3} → T_{0,3} → 1.
- π_{0,3} = π_1(U^an_{0,3}; -j̄) is free of rank 2.
- T_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2 is the group of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms of P^1 stabilising {0,1,∞}.
- Its holomorphic part S_3 is identified with the permutations of {0,1,∞}.
- Explicit Möbius formulas: σ̇0(z)=z/(z−1), σ̇1(z)=1/z, σ̇∞(z)=1−z (each the transposition fixing the indexed point), ρ̇(z)=1/(1−z) (the cycle 0→1→∞→0), ρ̇^{-1}(z)=(z−1)/z.
- Relations: σ̇0σ̇1=σ̇1σ̇∞=σ̇∞σ̇0=ρ̇; ρ̇σ̇_iρ̇^{-1} = σ̇ of the next index in the cyclic order 0→1→∞; σ̇_i² = ρ̇³ = 1.
- The Z/2 factor is the centre of T_{0,3}; the next page says it is generated by complex conjugation.

In modern terms this is the classical extension 1 → F_2 ≅ Γ̄(2) → PGL(2,Z) → S_3 × Z/2 → 1. Here Γ̄(2) is the principal congruence subgroup of level 2 modulo ±1, and S_3 ≅ PSL(2,F_2). The page sets up the finite-symmetry and real-structure bookkeeping used to state the GT-type 'loop equations' over the profinite completion.

The margin note suggests defining 𝔊_{0,3} intrinsically as a group of automorphisms of π_{0,3}. This is natural: the free group is centre-free, so the extension embeds into Aut(π_{0,3}), and Out(F_2) ≅ GL(2,Z) (Nielsen).
errors: No mathematical errors found: all Möbius formulas, fixed points of the transpositions, composition identities (3), conjugation identities and orders (4) check out, using the composition convention (fg)(z)=f(g(z)).

Minor notational looseness: the title identifies 𝔊_{0,3} (which includes the antiholomorphic Z/2) with the fundamental group of the orbifold P^1(2,3,∞). Strictly, PGL(2,Z) is the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient by S_3 × Z/2 including complex conjugation; PSL(2,Z) corresponds to the holomorphic part. Context and the tilde notation suggest Grothendieck means the extended version.

ideas.what: Explicit S_3 action on P^1 minus {0,1,∞} by the six anharmonic Möbius maps, with relations
𝔊_{0,3} as extension of S_3×Z/2 by π_1(P^1 minus 3 points) ≅ F_2, identified with PGL(2,Z) and with the extended mapping-class group of the once-punctured torus modulo ±1

ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, T_{0,3}, T_{1,1}); La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois

missed.claim: The margin suggests defining 𝔊_{0,3} intrinsically inside Aut(π_{0,3}), rather than via the topological extension, as the starting point for the profinite/Galois version. This is standard in the later GT literature, where GT is viewed inside Aut(F̂_2) normalising inertia. It is only a passing remark here and gives no new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: a historical trace of Grothendieck's intrinsic viewpoint, already absorbed by the GT literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A recap/conventions page of classical material: the anharmonic S_3 action, PGL(2,Z) as an extension of S_3×Z/2 by F_2, and the link with T_{1,1}. Its only historical interest is as context for Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type 'équation des lacets' computations on neighbouring pages; nothing new on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: Title: the middle term is better read as π_1(U^an_{0,3}, 𝔊̃_3 ; −j̄) (a tilde-decorated S_3, i.e. an equivariant/orbifold π_1), and the next term as π̃'_{0,3} ≃ π_1(P^{1an}, 0{0}+2{1}+3{∞}), {𝔊̃_3} ; −j̄.
In the second title line 'GP(1,Z)' is Grothendieck's notation for PGL(2,Z), the projective group of P^1 over Z, and '≃' links it to T'_{1,1} = T_{1,1}/{±1}.
The annotation above σ̇0 reads '= 1 + 1/(z−1)' (with a correction), consistent with z/(z−1).
The margin is only partially legible: roughly 'idée: 𝔊_{0,3} défini comme un Autom(π_{0,3}) — on a … (En fait, il y a une définition diff[érente?] … cf. ci-dessous)'.
